We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-type hierarchy, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. Across multiple simulated and real heterogeneous tissue datasets, HOMED achieved a 68% higher mean Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) and 60% lower mean root mean squared error (RMSE), compared to other scRNA-seq-guided or single-cell DNA methylation-based DNAm deconvolution methods. Moreover, application of HOMED to a smoking-exposed placenta DNA methylation cohort revealed significant shifts in cell-type compositions in endothelial, nRBC, stromal, and villous trophoblast proportions. Adjusting for these compositional differences reduced inflated smoking-associated CpGs by nearly three folds, and doubled the number of enriched pathways with known associations to smoking. In summary, HOMED is an accurate and practical method to infer cell-type proportions from bulk DNA methylation data.

papers.t: A unique intestinal epithelial cell that expresses canonical lymphoid genes.
papers.ab: Enterocytes and intestinal secretory cells harbor innate immunity. However, certain transcriptional programs -even beyond rearranged T- and B-cell receptor genes- are considered the exclusive purview of adaptive immune cells, including abundant and diverse intestinal intra-epithelial lymphocytes (IELs). Here, we identify and characterize columnar intestinal secretory cells that co-express classic epithelial and lymphoid genes, including Ptprc, Cd3e, Cd8a, and Gzma/b but not T- or B-cell receptors. These previously unrecognized epithelium-derived lymphoid-like cells (EDLCs) differ from any known resident cell type, including IELs or tuft cells. Rare in healthy mouse and human intestines, their numbers increase upon IL-25 stimulation or IL-10 receptor deficiency in vivo and upon IL-13 stimulation in vitro. EDLC chromatin is uniquely accessible at thousands of cis-elements, including lymphoid and epithelial loci. These findings reveal a transcriptionally and epigenetically distinct intestinal epithelial derivative that expresses prominent lymphoid character.

papers.t: Single-Nucleus Profiling Reveals Neuronal Metabolic Collapse During the Transition to Alzheimer's Disease Dementia.
papers.ab: Current Alzheimer's disease (AD) neuropathological metrics, including Thal phasing, and Braak staging, often do not accurately predict cognitive status: many cognitively resilient individuals have substantial pathological burdens, whereas some patients with dementia show minimal classical AD pathology. Here, we addressed this discrepancy by investigating the molecular mechanisms underlying AD dementia using single-nucleus RNA-sequencing and single-nucleus multiome datasets. To eliminate cross-modality scaling artifacts and compositional biases inherent in neurodegenerative tissues, we normalized the datasets using our novel framework, bypassing scaling issues of conventional methods that may obscure critical biological signals of interest. We identified neuron-specific suppression of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes and their upstream mitochondrial biogenesis signaling (MBS) as primary drivers of clinical dementia. By integrating multi-omic quantitative trait loci, genome-wide association studies, and epigenomic profiles, we delineated genetic and epigenetic changes underlying MBS suppression. This study provides a systematic genomic framework for understanding the mechanisms of cognitive resilience.

papers.t: A MultiOmics time-resolved systems map of gene regulation in Toxoplasma gondii.
papers.ab: Understanding how T. gondii builds an invasion-competent cell has been limited by its rapid, asynchronous division cycle, incomplete gene function annotation, and studies that have examined one regulator or complex at a time. Here, we placed acute perturbation of 21 transcriptional and epigenetic factors, promoter occupancy, chromatin accessibility, and molecular validation on a common single-cell clock. The resulting consensus map links the lytic-cycle programs to candidate activating and repressive inputs, organizes genes into 108 co-regulated communities, and nominates regulatory partnerships that would not have emerged from any single data type. The work bridges three longstanding gaps: it resolves perturbation responses in cell-cycle time, distinguishes promoter occupancy from perturbation-linked regulation, and turns a large multidimensional dataset into an experimentally navigable map. We indeed confirmed known factor interactions such as MORC/HDAC3, and recovered combinations such as the Cdc5/SNIP1 and DMAP1/EPL1 as coregulatory nodes (that in other systems have been described to cooperate). Furthermore, we discovered a novel apicomplexan specific combination of AAF1/AP2XI-5 that provides mechanistic insights of the unique AP2 transcription factor family.

papers.t: Influence of the male germline on B chromosome transmission in D. melanogaster.
papers.ab: Selfish genetic elements that bias their inheritance to the detriment to their host are in an evolutionary arms race with host-derived suppressors that neutralize the spread of these elements. The supernumerary B chromosomes recently found in a mutant Drosophila melanogaster laboratory stock are subject to drive (>50% transmission) when passed through the female germline, but through the male germline they experience the opposite of drive, a phenomenon referred to as drag (<50% transmission). Here we show that males from this mutant stock do not have fertility defects, excluding the possibility that sperm carrying more B chromosomes are inviable. Though we revealed irregularities in the germline stem cell (GSC) niche, we show that other aspects of GSCs activity is normal: there is no delay in their mitoses and the B chromosomes appear to be symmetrically segregated during the GSC divisions, suggesting that the asymmetry of these divisions is not likely the source of B chromosome drag. Together, this work lays the foundation for future studies into the mechanism of paternal B chromosome drag in D. melanogaster , which is poised to significantly advance on our understanding of how various genetic and developmental contexts promote disparate chromosome behavior.

papers.t: Modeling of human MLH1 and MLH3 variants in mice reveals novel functions of MutLγ in meiotic DNA repair and the ovarian reserve.
papers.ab: The mismatch repair proteins MLH1 and MLH3 form the MutLγ complex that is essential for >90% of meiotic crossovers (CO) in mice. Although deletion of either gene causes infertility, we previously found that mouse models of certain human MLH1/3 missense variants caused elevated aneuploidy and progressive loss of female fecundity despite having a normal ovarian reserve. Here, we report that additional missense and null alleles caused significant pre-pubertal follicle loss independent of alterations to meiotic CO levels. Deletion of the DNA damage checkpoint kinase Chek2 (Chk2) partially rescued the oocyte pool of Mlh1- and Mlh3 -deficient mice, indicating that defects in meiotic prophase I triggered oocyte elimination. In spermatocytes, both missense and null alleles caused abnormal γH2AX 'flares' on autosomes during late pachynema and diplonema, extending into chromatin loops from the synaptonemal complex. These flares frequently contained unusually large foci of the ssDNA binding protein RPA as well as DNA end processing factors including CtIP, RAD50 and BLM, consistent with abnormal and extensive DNA resection. The results reveal a previously unrecognized meiotic function of MutLγ in preventing DNA hyper-resection of spontaneous DNA breaks or of persistent recombination intermediates in late prophase I. Together with our previous studies, the results show that MLH1/3 variants can impair fertility through at least three mechanistically distinct routes: severe crossover loss sufficient to activate the metaphase I spindle assembly checkpoint; subthreshold crossover defects that increase aneuploidy and embryo loss; and abnormal late-prophase DNA processing that activates a CHEK2-dependent oocyte quality-control pathway and depletes the ovarian reserve, causing primary ovarian insufficiency (POI). Thus, MutLγ has broader roles in maintaining meiotic genome integrity than can be explained by crossover formation alone.

papers.t: LongVerse: verified AI agents for Nanopore and PacBio DNA methylation analysis.
papers.ab: AI agents now run sequencing pipelines, but their outputs are checked by rubrics or language-model judges, not against an independent measurement. LongVerse turns one English sentence into haplotype-resolved DNA methylation from Nanopore or PacBio reads, through agents that read the data, supply arguments to a pinned pipeline and never write code. On HG002, a healthy reference genome, agent and human expert produced byte-identical calls (r = 1.000) that agreed with bisulfite sequencing (r = 0.943, 0.884), at $0.12 to $0.54 of conversation per run. A consensus agent that admits any per-site caller reduced error 10.7 percent against the best published caller.

papers.t: cBAF drives AR-V7 expression through regulation of transcriptional termination in castration-resistant prostate cancer.
papers.ab: UNLABELLED: The androgen receptor splice variant AR-V7 drives resistance to androgen receptor-targeted therapies in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), but the mechanisms governing its expression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the canonical BAF (cBAF) chromatin remodeling complex as a selective regulator of AR-V7 expression. Pharmacologic and genetic disruption of cBAF reduced AR-V7 levels, suppressed AR-V7-dependent transcriptional programs, and impaired CRPC cell proliferation. Mechanistically, cBAF binds an intronic regulatory element downstream of AR cryptic exon 3, where it maintains chromatin accessibility, enhancer activity, and promoter-enhancer looping. cBAF loss decreases recruitment of transcription termination machinery, reduces RNA polymerase II Thr4 phosphorylation, and promotes transcriptional readthrough beyond the AR-V7 polyadenylation site. POINT-seq revealed that cBAF-dependent transcriptional termination is required for AR-V7 biogenesis and regulates termination at a subset of genes genome-wide. Together, these findings uncover a role for cBAF in chromatin-mediated control of transcriptional termination and establish this mechanism as a critical determinant of AR-V7 expression. KEY FINDINGS: cBAF is the only SWI/SNF subcomplex required for AR-V7 expression and function.AR-V7 transcription requires cBAF-promoted premature transcriptional termination in addition to alternative splicing.cBAF maintains an intronic enhancer-like regulatory element through chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac, and chromatin looping.cBAF broadly influences RNA polymerase II termination dynamics, revealing a previously unrecognized role in transcriptional termination.

papers.t: Early-onset spontaneous murine mammary tumors show increased lymphocyte representation and reduced MHC antigen presentation.
papers.ab: SIMPLE SUMMARY: Not all breast tumors behave the same way, and part of the reason may be inherited rather than caused by the tumor itself. Using mice that carry the same cancer-causing HER2/neu gene but differ in genetic background, we found that introduction of the PWK/PhJ genetic background was associated with tumors that appeared about a month earlier. These early tumors contained a larger proportion of immune cells, including T and B cells, but the T-cell population showed reduced expression of genes associated with cytotoxic activity. At the same time, the tumors had lower levels of proteins and genes that let the immune system recognize tumor cells, alongside higher levels of structural proteins that can make tissue stiffer and easier for cancer to invade. These findings suggest that genetic background shapes not only how quickly breast tumors arise but also how well the immune system can recognize them, a distinction that may matter for future immune-based treatments. BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Genetic background modifies cancer risk and phenotype in humans, but its influence on the tumor immune microenvironment and antigen-presentation machinery in ErbB2 (HER2/neu)-driven breast cancer is not well defined. We used a genetically diverse mouse cross to test whether the wild-derived PWK/PhJ background alters immune infiltration and antigen presentation in a NeuT model of HER2/neu-positive breast cancer. METHODS: Previously, quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping using Diversity Outbred mice and r/qtl2 identified candidate loci driving tumor onset and growth. The wild-derived PWK/PhJ genetic background was predicted to harbor genes that regulated early onset of HER2/neu-driven tumors. BALB NeuT and (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT female mice were monitored twice weekly for spontaneous mammary tumor onset and growth. Tumor immune composition was profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. Protein abundance was measured by data-independent acquisition proteomics in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tumor tissue (n=5 per genotype). Single-nucleus multiome (RNA + ATAC), bulk RNA-seq, and H3K27ac datasets from the same strain comparison were analyzed for focused MHC II cross-layer analyses. RESULTS: As predicted, (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT mice developed tumors significantly earlier than the parental BALB NeuT mice (10 vs. 14-15 weeks of age; p < 0.0001). In the scRNA-seq dataset, F1 tumors showed greater representation of Cd3e -expressing T cells and a Cd79a -expressing B-cell population not detected in BALB NeuT tumors, and a distinct neutrophil cluster; F1 T cells also showed lower expression of the cytotoxicity-associated genes Tox, Ltk, Nkg7 , and Gzmb relative to BALB NeuT tumor-infiltrating T cells. Proteomics identified 46 differentially abundant proteins (25 higher, 21 lower in F1), with coordinate down-regulation of Stat1, Tapbp, Parp9 , and Dtx3l alongside MHC class I and II proteins and up-regulation of extracellular-matrix and elastic-fiber proteins. Focused cross-layer analysis showed lower whole-tumor expression of a Stat1 /MHC II-associated gene set together with reduced epithelial chromatin accessibility at selected regions near Cd74 and H2-Aa . CONCLUSIONS: The PWK/PhJ genetic background is associated with earlier HER2-driven tumor onset, greater lymphocyte representation, and reduced activity of a STAT1-associated antigen-presentation program despite similar post-onset tumor growth kinetics.

papers.t: Histone modifications define distinct nucleosome positions in cell-free DNA.
papers.ab: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentation patterns reflect nucleosome positioning. We asked whether variation in nucleosome positions in cfDNA can reveal chromatin states and associated histone modifications. Using cell-free chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (cfChIP-seq) in plasma from patients with prostate cancer, we identified 35,120 modification-associated positions (MAPs), loci where nucleosomes bearing active (H3K4me2) and repressive (H3K9me3) histone marks occupy reproducibly offset positions. These offsets recurred across histone marks, an independent cfChIP-seq cohort, and nuclease-digested chromatin from cell lines. MAPs were enriched in transcribed genes but depleted near transcription start sites and CTCF-binding sites where nucleosome positioning is constrained. Across 2,535 cfDNA sequencing datasets, nucleosome protection at a subset of MAPs correlated with tumor fraction (TF), reflecting differences in histone modification status between cancer-derived and non-malignant chromatin. In targeted sequencing panels, a 50-MAP model using fragments from < 0.001% of the genome distinguished samples with tumor fractions ≥3% vs 0% (AUCs = 0.91-0.96 across prostate, breast, and lung cancers) and outperformed a state-of-the-art fragmentomics-based tumor fraction predictor. MAP-derived estimates correlated with reference TFs (r = 0.89) and longitudinal changes in TF (r = 0.91). MAP protection at ASCL1 binding sites identified neuroendocrine transformation of prostate cancer from cfDNA. These findings establish histone-modification-associated nucleosome positioning as a mutation-independent readout of tumor fraction and cancer state from routine cfDNA sequencing.

papers.t: Engineered Tn5 Variants Enhance CUT&Tag Fidelity for Transcription Factors.
papers.ab: The CUT&Tag method performs exceptionally well for profiling histone modifications, but mapping sequence-specific transcription factors (TFs) is complicated by intrinsic Tn5 activity at accessible DNA, and the high-salt washes used to suppress this activity can destabilize TF-chromatin interactions. We engineered the Tn5 DNA-binding channel to attenuate target-DNA engagement by replacing individual positively charged amino acids with neutral amino acids. We identified a "Goldilocks" variant (K160A) with intermediate attenuation that improved recovery of GATA2 motif-containing sites under low-salt CUT&Tag and KCl-based DynaTag conditions. A second variant (K249A) had improved performance for profiling CTCF over less accessible sites characterized by sharply focused short-fragment enrichment. By comparing the K160A and K249A variants, this TF-CUT&Tag assay provides a physical readout of the local chromatin environment at TF binding sites. Applying K160A TF-CUT&Tag to pluripotency-associated TFs in mouse embryonic stem cells increased recovery across their genomic binding landscapes while preserving factor-specific motif architectures. During skeletal muscle differentiation, TF-CUT&Tag improved recovery of MyoG and Pax7 occupancy relative to standard CUT&Tag, revealing strongly motif-enriched MyoG binding and a shift in Pax7 binding from CpG-rich promoters in progenitors toward Pax7 motif-enriched sites during differentiation. Together, these results show that TF-CUT&Tag captures distinct modes of TF- chromatin interaction, including motif-directed binding sites and more salt-sensitive sites that may depend on lower-affinity DNA recognition or protein-protein interactions and are difficult to predict from DNA sequence alone.

papers.t: Histone modifications directly modulate transcription factor binding to nucleosomes.
papers.ab: Transcription factors (TFs) that can recognize specific DNA sequences within nucleosomes play key roles in regulating cell fate transitions, but what regulates their condition-dependent binding to nucleosomes remains poorly understood. Here, we determined the direct effects of H3K27ac, H3K27me3 and H3K9me3 on binding by 7 human TFs to a highly diverse library of nucleosomes. We found that these marks influence the preference of FOXA1 and PAX7 to bind as monomers versus dimers to nucleosomes. Furthermore, H3K27ac impairs TF binding at internal regions of nucleosomes, enhancing end-binding preferences, for most of the assayed TFs. Our results suggest that histone marks represent an additional layer of cis-regulatory encoding that directly regulates TF interactions with nucleosomal binding sites.
